verses.8: God reigneth over the nations: / God sitteth upon his holy throne.
verses.9: The princes of the peoples are gathered together, / with the people of the God of Abraham;
verses.10: For the rulers of the earth belong unto God; / he is very highly exalted.

verses.1: Great is the LORD, and highly to be praised / in the city of our God.
verses.2: His holy hill is a fair place, / and the joy of the whole earth:
verses.3: Mount Sion of the uttermost parts of the north, / the city of the great King.
verses.4: He hath made himself known in her citadels / as a sure refuge.
verses.5: For lo, the kings of the earth were gathered, / and gone by together.
verses.6: They marvelled to see such things; / they were astonished, and suddenly cast down.
verses.7: Fear came there upon them, / and anguish, as upon a woman in her travail;
verses.8: As when with the east wind / thou breakest the ships of the sea.
verses.9: Like as we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the LORD of hosts, in the city of our God: / God upholdeth the same for ever.
verses.10: We have thought on thy loving-kindness, O God, / in the midst of thy temple.
verses.11: O God, according to thy Name, so is thy praise unto the world’s end; / thy right hand is full of righteousness.
verses.12: Let the mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Judah be glad, / because of thy judgements.
verses.13: Walk about Sion, and go round about her; / and count the towers thereof.
verses.14: Mark well her bulwarks, consider her citadels, / that ye may tell them that come after.
verses.15: For this God is our God for ever and ever: / he shall be our guide for evermore.

verses.1: O Hear ye this, all ye peoples; / ponder it with your ears, all ye that dwell in the world;
verses.2: High and low, rich and poor, / one with another.
verses.3: My mouth shall speak of wisdom, / and my heart shall muse of understanding.
verses.4: I will incline mine ear to a parable, / and expound my dark speech upon the harp.
verses.5: Wherefore should I fear in the days of wickedness, / when the wickedness of my foes compasseth me round about?
verses.6: There be some that put their trust in their wealth, / and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches.
verses.7: But no man can by any means redeem his brother, / nor give a ransom unto God for him,
verses.8: That he should live on for ever, / and see not the grave.
verses.9: For too costly is the redemption of their souls, / so that he must let that alone for ever.
verses.10: For he seeth that wise men also die, and perish together, / as well as the ignorant and foolish, and leave their riches for others.
verses.11: Their graves are their homes for ever, and their dwelling-places to all generations; / even though they called lands after their own names.
verses.12: So man being in honour abideth not; / he is like the beasts that perish.
verses.13: This is the fate of them that are foolishly confident, / and the latter end of them that are pleased with their portion.
verses.14: Like sheep they are appointed for the grave; death is their shepherd; / and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning.
verses.15: Their beauty shall waste away in the sepulchre; / there shall be no habitation for it.
verses.16: But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave; / for he shall receive me.
verses.17: Be not thou afraid, though one be made rich, / or if the glory of his house be increased;
verses.18: For he shall carry nothing away with him when he dieth, / neither shall his pomp follow him.
verses.19: For though while he lived, he counted himself a happy man; / and men praise thee because thou doest well unto thyself;
verses.20: Yet he shall follow the generation of his fathers, / and shall never see light.
verses.21: Man that is in honour, but hath no understanding, / is like the beasts that perish.

verses.1: The LORD, even the Most Mighty God, hath spoken, / and called the world, from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
verses.2: Out of Sion, the perfection of beauty, / God hath shined forth.
verses.3: Our God cometh, and keepeth not silence; / there goeth before him a consuming fire, and a mighty tempest is stirred up round about him.
verses.4: He calleth to the heavens from above, / and to the earth, that he may judge his people:
verses.5: ‘Gather my saints together unto me: / those that have made a covenant with me with sacrifice.’
verses.6: And the heavens declare his righteousness; / for God is judge himself.
verses.7: ‘Hear, O my people, and I will speak; / I myself will testify against thee, O Israel; for I am God, even thy God.
verses.8: I will not reprove thee because of thy sacrifices; / as for thy burnt offerings, they are alway before me.
verses.9: I will take no bullock out of thine house, / nor he-goats out of thy folds.
verses.10: For all the beasts of the forest are mine, / and so are the cattle upon a thousand hills.
verses.11: I know all the birds upon the mountains, / and the wild beasts of the field are in my sight.
verses.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell thee; / for the whole world is mine, and all that is therein.
verses.13: Thinkest thou that I will eat bulls’ flesh, / and drink the blood of goats?
verses.14: Offer unto God the sacrifice of thanksgiving, / and pay thy vows unto the Most High;
verses.15: And call upon me in the time of trouble; / so will I deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.’
verses.16: But unto the ungodly saith God, / ‘Why dost thou preach my laws, and takest my covenant in thy mouth;
verses.17: Whereas thou hatest to be reformed, / and hast cast my words behind thee?
verses.18: When thou sawest a thief, thou consentedst unto him, / and hast been partaker with the adulterers.
verses.19: Thou dost let thy mouth speak wickedness, / and with thy tongue thou dost set forth deceit.
verses.20: Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother, / and dost slander thine own mother’s son.
verses.21: These things hast thou done, and I held my tongue, and thou thoughtest that I am even such a one as thyself; / but I will reprove thee, and set before thee the things that thou hast done.
verses.22: O Consider this, ye that forget God, / lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.
verses.23: Whoso offereth me the sacrifice of thanksgiving, he honoureth me; / and to him that ordereth his way aright will I show the salvation of God.’

verses.1: Have mercy upon me, O God, after thy great goodness; / according to the multitude of thy mercies do away mine offences.
verses.2: Wash me throughly from my wickedness, / and cleanse me from my sin.
verses.3: For I acknowledge my faults, / and my sin is ever before me.
verses.4: Against thee only have I sinned, and done that which is evil in thy sight; / that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and clear when thou dost judge.
verses.5: Behold, I was brought forth in wickedness, / and in sin hath my mother conceived me.
verses.6: But lo, thou requirest truth in the inward parts, / and shalt make me to understand wisdom secretly.
verses.7: Thou shalt purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; / thou shalt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
verses.8: Thou shalt make me hear of joy and gladness, / that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
verses.9: Turn thy face from my sins, / and put out all my misdeeds.
verses.10: Make me a clean heart, O God, / and renew a right spirit within me.
verses.11: Cast me not away from thy presence, / and take not thy holy spirit from me.
verses.12: O give me the comfort of thy help again, / and stablish me with a free spirit.
verses.13: Then shall I teach thy ways unto the wicked, / and sinners shall be converted unto thee.
verses.14: Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, thou that art the God of my salvation; / and my tongue shall sing of thy righteousness.
verses.15: O Lord, open thou my lips, / and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.
verses.16: For thou desirest no sacrifice, else would I give it; / but thou delightest not in burnt offerings.
verses.17: The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit: / a broken and contrite heart, O God, shalt thou not despise.
verses.18: O Be favourable and gracious unto Sion; / build thou the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.19: Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with the burnt offerings and oblations; / then shall they offer young bullocks upon thine altar.

verses.1: Why boastest thou thyself, thou tyrant, that thou canst do mischief, / whereas the goodness of God endureth yet daily?
verses.2: Thy tongue deviseth wickedness; / it is like a sharp razor, O thou worker of deceit.
verses.3: Thou hast loved evil more than goodness, / and to speak lies rather than righteousness.
verses.4: Thou hast loved to speak all words that may do hurt, / O thou false tongue.
verses.5: Therefore shall God destroy thee for ever; / he shall take thee and pluck thee out of thy dwelling, and root thee out of the land of the living.
verses.6: The righteous also shall see this, and fear, / and shall laugh him to scorn,
verses.7: Saying, ‘Lo, this is the man that took not God for his strength, / but trusted unto the multitude of his riches, and strengthened himself in his own wealth.’
verses.8: As for me, I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God; / my trust is in the tender mercy of God for ever and ever.
verses.9: I will always give thanks unto thee, because thou hast done it; / and I will hope in thy Name, for thy saints like it well.

verses.1: The foolish body hath said in his heart, / ‘There is no God.’
verses.2: Corrupt are they, and become abominable in their wickedness; / there is none that doeth good.
verses.3: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, / to see if there were any that would understand, and seek after God.
verses.4: But they are all gone out of the way; together they are become abominable; / there is also none that doeth good, no not one.
verses.5: Are they not without understanding that work wickedness, / eating up my people as if they would eat bread? they have not called upon God.
verses.6: There were they afraid, where no fear was; / for God hath scattered the bones of him that besieged thee: thou hast put them to confusion, because God hath despised them.
verses.7: O That salvation for Israel were come out of Sion! / When God restoreth the fortunes of his people,
verses.8: Then shall Jacob rejoice, / and Israel shall be right glad.

verses.1: Save me, O God, for thy Name’s sake, / and avenge me in thy strength.
verses.2: Hear my prayer, O God, / and hearken unto the words of my mouth.
verses.3: For strangers are risen up against me; / and tyrants, who have not God before their eyes, seek after my soul.
verses.4: Behold, God is my helper: / the Lord is he that upholdeth my soul.
verses.5: He shall reward evil unto mine enemies: / destroy thou them in thy truth.
verses.6: A Free-Will offering will I give to thee, / and praise thy Name, O LORD, because it is so comfortable.
verses.7: For he hath delivered me out of all my trouble; / and mine eye hath seen its desire upon mine enemies.

verses.1: Hear my prayer, O God, / and hide not thyself from my petition.
verses.2: Take heed unto me, and hear me, / how I mourn in my prayer, and am vexed.
verses.3: The enemy crieth so, and the ungodly cometh on so fast; / for they are minded to do me some mischief; so maliciously are they set against me.
verses.4: My heart is disquieted within me, / and the terrors of death are fallen upon me.
verses.5: Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, / and an horrible dread hath overwhelmed me.
verses.6: And I said, ‘O that I had wings like a dove! / for then would I fly away, and be at rest.
verses.7: Lo, then would I get me away far off, / and abide in the wilderness.
verses.8: I would make haste to find me a shelter / from the stormy wind and tempest.’
verses.9: Destroy their tongues, O Lord, and divide them; / for I have spied violence and strife in the city.
verses.10: Day and night they go about it, upon the walls thereof: / iniquity also and mischief are in the midst of it.
verses.11: Wickedness is therein: / oppression and guile go not out of her streets.
verses.12: For it is not an open enemy, that hath done me this dishonour; / for then I could have borne it;
verses.13: Neither was it mine adversary, that did magnify himself against me; / for then I would have hid myself from him.
verses.14: But it was even thou, my companion, / my guide, and mine own familiar friend.
verses.15: We took sweet counsel together, / and walked in the house of God as friends.
verses.16: As for me, I will call upon God, / and the LORD shall save me.
verses.17: In the evening, and morning, and at noonday will I pray, and that instantly; / and he shall hear my voice.
verses.18: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me; / for there were many that strove with me.
verses.19: Yea, even God, that endureth for ever, shall hear me, and bring them down; / for they will not turn, nor fear God.
verses.20: He laid his hands upon such as were at peace with him, / and he brake his covenant.
verses.21: His speech was smoother than butter, yet war was in his heart; / his words were softer than oil, yet be they very swords.
verses.22: O cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall uphold thee, / and shall not suffer the righteous to be moved for ever.
verses.23: But as for them, thou, O God, shalt bring them down / into the pit of destruction.
verses.24: The bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; / but my trust shall be in thee.

verses.1: Be merciful unto me, O God, for man goeth about to devour me: / he is all the day long fighting and troubling me.
verses.2: Mine enemies go about all the day long to swallow me up; / for they be many that fight proudly against me.
verses.3: Nevertheless, though I am sometime afraid, / yet put I my trust in thee.
verses.4: I will praise God because of his word: I have put my trust in God, and will not be afraid; / what can flesh do unto me?
verses.5: All the the day long they mistake my words: / all that they imagine is to do me evil.
verses.6: They hold all together, and keep themselves close, / and mark my steps, as they lay wait for my soul.
verses.7: Shall they escape by their wickedness? / O God, in thy displeasure cast down the peoples.
verses.8: Thou keepest count of my wanderings; put my tears into thy bottle: / are not these things noted in thy book?
verses.9: Whensoever I call upon thee, then shall mine enemies be put to flight: / this I know; for God is on my side.
verses.10: In God’s word will I rejoice: / in the LORD’ S word will I comfort me.
verses.11: Yea, in God have I put my trust, and will not be afraid; / what can man do unto me?
verses.12: Unto thee, O God, will I pay my vows: / unto thee will I give thanks.
verses.13: For thou hast delivered my soul from death, and my feet from falling, / that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

verses.1: Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me; / for my soul trusteth in thee;
verses.2: And under the shadow of thy wings shall be my refuge, / until this tyranny be overpast.
verses.3: I will call unto God Most High, / even unto the God that shall perform the cause that I have in hand.
verses.4: He shall send from heaven and save me, / even from the reproach of him that would eat me up.
verses.5: God shall send forth his mercy and truth; / my soul is among lions;
verses.6: And I lie even among the children of men, that are set on fire, / whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
verses.7: Set up thyself, O God, above the heavens, / and thy glory above all the earth.
verses.8: They have laid a net for my feet, and pressed down my soul; / they have digged a pit before me, and are fallen into the midst of it themselves.
verses.9: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready; / I will sing and give praise.
verses.10: Awake up, my soul; awake, lute and harp: / I myself will awake the dawn.
verses.11: I will give thanks unto thee, O Lord, among the peoples; / and I will sing unto thee among the nations.
verses.12: For the greatness of thy mercy reacheth unto the heavens, / and thy truth unto the clouds.
verses.13: Set up thyself, O God, above the heavens, / and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.1: Deliver me from mine enemies, O God; / defend me from them that rise up against me.
verses.2: O deliver me from the wicked doers, / and save me from the bloodthirsty men.
verses.3: For lo, they lie waiting for my soul; / the mighty men are gathered against me, without any offence or fault of me, O LORD.
verses.4: For no iniquity of mine they run and prepare themselves; / arise thou therefore to help me, and behold.
verses.5: For thou, O LORD of hosts, art the God of Israel; stand up to visit all the nations; / and be not merciful unto them that offend of malicious wickedness.
verses.6: They return in the evening; they snarl like a dog, / and go round about the city.
verses.7: Behold, they boast with their mouths, and swords are in their lips; / ‘For who’, say they, ‘doth hear?’
verses.8: But thou, O LORD, shalt have them in derision: / and thou shalt laugh all the nations to scorn.
verses.9: O my Strength, I will wait upon thee; / for thou, O God, art my refuge.
verses.10: My God of his goodness shall come to meet me; / and God shall let me see my desire upon mine enemies.
verses.11: Slay them not, lest my people forget it; / but scatter them abroad by thy power, and put them down, O Lord, our defence.
verses.12: For the sin of their mouth, and for the words of their lips, let them be taken in their pride;/ and why? their talking is of cursing and lies.
verses.13: Consume them in thy wrath, consume them, that they be no more, / and that men may know that it is God that ruleth in Jacob, and unto the ends of the world.
verses.14: They return in the evening; they snarl like a dog, / and go round about the city.
verses.15: They run here and there for food, / and growl if they be not satisfied.
verses.16: As for me, I will sing of thy power, and will praise thy mercy betimes in the morning; / for thou hast been my defence, and a refuge in the day of my trouble.
verses.17: O my Strength, I will sing unto thee; / for thou, O God, art my refuge, and my merciful God.

verses.1: O God, thou hast cast us out, and broken us down: / thou hast also been displeased; O turn thee unto us again.
verses.2: Thou hast made the land to tremble, and hast rent it: / heal the breaches thereof, for it shaketh.
verses.3: Thou hast showed thy people heavy things: / thou hast given us a drink of deadly wine.
verses.4: Thou hast given a banner for such as fear thee, / that they may flee from the bow.
verses.5: That thy beloved may be delivered, / help me with thy right hand, and hear me.
verses.6: God hath spoken in his holiness: ‘I will rejoice, and divide Shechem, / and mete out the valley of Succoth.
verses.7: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; / Ephraim also is the defence of my head; Judah is my sceptre;
verses.8: Moab is my wash-pot; upon Edom will I cast out my shoe; / over Philistia will I shout in triumph.’
verses.9: Who will lead me into the strong city? / who will bring me into Edom?
verses.10: Hast thou not cast us out, O God? / and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts?
verses.11: O be thou our help in trouble; / for vain is the help of man.
verses.12: Through God we shall do great acts; / for it is he that will tread down our enemies.

verses.1: Hear my crying, O God, / give ear unto my prayer.
verses.2: From the end of the earth will I call upon thee, when my heart is in heaviness: / O lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
verses.3: For thou hast been my refuge, / and a strong tower for me against the enemy.
verses.4: I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever, / and my trust shall be under the covering of thy wings.
verses.5: For thou, O God, hast heard my desires, / and hast given an heritage unto those that fear thy Name.
verses.6: Thou shalt grant the king a long life: / his years shall be as many generations.
verses.7: He shall dwell before God for ever; / O prepare thy loving mercy and faithfulness, that they may preserve him.
verses.8: So will I alway sing praise unto thy Name, / that I may daily perform my vows.

verses.1: My soul truly waiteth in silence upon God; / for of him cometh my salvation.
verses.2: He verily is my strength and my salvation; / he is my defence, so that I shall not greatly fall.
verses.3: How long will ye set upon a man, battering him, all of you, / like a tottering wall, and like a broken fence?
verses.4: Their device is only how to put him out whom God will exalt; / their delight is in lies; they give good words with their mouth, but curse with their heart.
verses.5: Nevertheless, my soul, wait thou in silence upon God; / for my hope is in him.
verses.6: He truly is my strength and my salvation; / he is my defence, so that I shall not fall.
verses.7: In God is my health and my glory: / the rock of my might, and in God is my trust.
verses.8: O put your trust in him alway, ye people: / pour out your hearts before him, for God is our hope.
verses.9: As for the sons of men, they are but vanity; yea, the sons of men are a deceit; / upon the scales they are altogether lighter than vanity itself.
verses.10: O trust not in wrong and robbery, give not yourselves unto vanity; / if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
verses.11: God spake once, and twice I have also heard the same, / that power belongeth unto God;
verses.12: And that thou, Lord, art merciful; / for thou renderest unto every man according to his work.

verses.1: O God, thou art my God; / early will I seek thee.
verses.2: My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh also longeth after thee, / in a barren and dry land, where no water is.
verses.3: Thus have I looked upon thee in the sanctuary, / that I might behold thy power and glory.
verses.4: For thy loving-kindness is better than the life itself: / my lips shall praise thee.
verses.5: As long as I live will I magnify thee in this manner, / and lift up my hands in thy Name.
verses.6: My soul shall be satisfied, even as it were with marrow and fatness; / and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.
verses.7: When I remember thee upon my bed, / I meditate upon thee in the night-watches;
verses.8: Because thou hast been my helper; / and under the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
verses.9: My soul cleaveth unto thee; / thy right hand upholdeth me.
verses.10: These also that seek the hurt of my soul, / they shall go into the depths of the earth.
verses.11: They shall be given over to the power of the sword, / that they may be a portion for foxes.
verses.12: But the king shall rejoice in God; all they that swear by him shall be glad; / for the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.

verses.1: Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: / preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
verses.2: Hide me from the secret council of the wicked, / and from the throng of evil doers;
verses.3: Who have whet their tongue like a sword, / and aimed their arrows, even bitter words;
verses.4: That they may privily shoot at him that is perfect: / suddenly do they shoot at him and fear not.
verses.5: They encourage themselves in mischief, / and commune among themselves how they may lay snares, and say that no man shall see them.
verses.6: They imagine wickedness, and practise it; / and the inward thought and heart of every one of them is deep.
verses.7: But God shall shoot at them with a swift arrow, / and suddenly shall they be smitten.
verses.8: Yea, their own tongue shall make them fall; / insomuch that whoso seeth them shall laugh them to scorn.
verses.9: And all men shall fear, and they shall tell what God hath done; / for they shall perceive that it is his work.
verses.10: The righteous shall rejoice in the LORD, and put his trust in him; / and all they that are true of heart shall be glad.

verses.1: Praise is due to thee, O God, in Sion; / and unto thee shall the vow be performed in Jerusalem.
verses.2: Thou that hearest the prayer, / unto thee shall all flesh come.
verses.3: My misdeeds prevail against me: / O be thou merciful unto our sins.
verses.4: Blessed is the man whom thou choosest and receivest, / that he may dwell in thy courts.
verses.5: We shall be satisfied with the pleasures of thy house, / even of thy holy temple.
verses.6: Thou shalt show us wonderful things in thy righteousness, O God of our salvation, / thou that art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that remain in the broad sea;
verses.7: Who in his strength setteth fast the mountains, / and is girded about with power;
verses.8: Who stilleth the raging of the seas, / the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
verses.9: They also that dwell in the uttermost parts of the earth are afraid at thy tokens, / thou that makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to praise thee.
verses.10: Thou visitest the earth and waterest it: / thou makest it very plenteous.
verses.11: The river of God is full of water: / thou preparest their grain, for so thou providest for the earth.
verses.12: Thou waterest her furrows, smoothing the ridges thereof: / thou makest it soft with the drops of rain, and blessest the increase of it.
verses.13: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; / and thy paths drip with fatness.
verses.14: The pastures of the wilderness drip; / and the little hills rejoice on every side.
verses.15: The pastures are clothed with flocks: / the valleys also stand so thick with grain that they laugh and sing.

verses.1: O Be joyful in God, all ye lands; / sing praises unto the honour of his Name; make his praise to be glorious.
verses.2: Say unto God, ‘O how wonderful are thy works! / because of the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies feign obedience unto thee.
verses.3: All the world shall worship thee, / sing of thee, and praise thy Name.’
verses.4: O Come hither, and behold the works of God: / how wonderful he is in his doing toward the children of men.
verses.5: He turned the sea into dry land, / so that they went through the water on foot; there did we rejoice in him.
verses.6: He ruleth with his power for ever; his eyes keep watch upon the nations: / let not such as be rebellious exalt themselves.
verses.7: O Praise our God, ye peoples,/ and make the voice of his praise to be heard;
verses.8: Who holdeth our soul in life, / and suffereth not our feet to slip.
verses.9: For thou, O God, hast proved us: / thou also hast tried us, like as silver is tried.
verses.10: Thou didst bring us into the snare, / and didst lay trouble upon our loins.
verses.11: Thou didst suffer men to ride over our heads: / we went through fire and water, but thou didst bring us out into a place of freedom.
verses.12: I Will go into thine house with burnt offerings: / I will pay thee my vows,
verses.13: Which I promised with my lips, / and spake with my mouth when I was in trouble.
verses.14: I will offer unto thee fat burnt sacrifices, with the incense of rams: / I will offer bullocks and goats.
verses.15: O come hither, and hearken, all ye that fear God, / and I will tell you what he hath done for my soul.
verses.16: I called unto him with my mouth, / and gave him praises with my tongue.
verses.17: If I had regarded wickedness in my heart, / the Lord would not have heard me.
verses.18: But verily God hath heard me, / and considered the voice of my prayer.
verses.19: Praised be God, who hath not cast out my prayer, / nor turned his mercy from me.

verses.1: God be merciful unto us, and bless us, / and show us the light of his countenance, and be merciful unto us;
verses.2: That thy way may be known upon earth, / thy saving health among all nations.
verses.3: Let the people praise thee, O God; / yea, let all the people praise thee.
verses.4: O Let the nations rejoice and be glad; / for thou shalt judge the folk righteously, and govern the nations upon earth.
verses.5: Let the people praise thee, O God; / yea, let all the people praise thee.
verses.6: The earth hath brought forth her increase; / and God, even our own God, shall give us his blessing.
verses.7: God shall bless us; / and all the ends of the world shall fear him.

verses.1: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: / let them also that hate him flee before him.
verses.2: Like as the smoke vanisheth, so shalt thou drive them away; / and like as wax melteth at the fire, so let the ungodly perish at the presence of God.
verses.3: But let the righteous be glad and rejoice before God: / let them also be merry and joyful.
verses.4: O Sing unto God, and sing praises unto his Name: / magnify him that rideth upon the heavens; praise him in his Name JAH, and rejoice before him.
verses.5: He is a father of the fatherless, and defendeth the cause of the widows: / even God in his holy habitation.
verses.6: He is the God that giveth the desolate a home to dwell in, and bringeth the prisoners out of captivity; / but the rebellious dwell in scarceness.
verses.7: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people, / when thou wentest through the wilderness,
verses.8: The earth shook, and the heavens poured down rain at the presence of God: / Sinai also quaked at the presence of God, who is the God of Israel.
verses.9: Thou, O God, sentest a gracious rain upon thine inheritance, / and refreshedst it when it was weary.
verses.10: Thy congregation dwelt therein; / for thou, O God, of thy goodness didst provide for the poor.
verses.11: The Lord gave the word; / and great was the host of the women that published the tidings:
verses.12: ‘Kings with their armies do flee, lo, they flee, / and she that tarrieth at home divideth the spoil.
verses.13: Though ye may lie among the sheep-folds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, / and her pinions with yellow gold.
verses.14: When the Almighty scattered kings therein, / then snow fell on Salmon.’
verses.15: The hill of Bashan is a mighty hill; / even an high hill is the hill of Bashan.
verses.16: Why look ye askance, ye high hills, at the hill which God hath desired for his abode? / yea, the LORD will abide in it for ever.
verses.17: The chariots of God are ten thousands, yea, even thousands upon thousands; / and the Lord is among them, as in the holy place of Sinai.
verses.18: Thou art gone up on high, thou hast led captivity captive, and received gifts among men, / yea, even among the rebellious, that the LORD God might dwell with them.
verses.19: Blessed be the Lord, who daily beareth our burden, / even the God who is our salvation.
verses.20: He is our God, even the God of whom cometh deliverance; / and GOD is the Lord by whom we escape death.
verses.21: It is well seen, O God, how thou goest, / how thou, my God and King, goest into the sanctuary.
verses.22: The singers go before, the minstrels follow after, / in the midst are the damsels playing with the timbrels:
verses.23: ‘Bless ye God in the congregations, / even the LORD, ye that are of the fountain of Israel.’
verses.24: There is little Benjamin their ruler, the princes of Judah and their company, / the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
verses.25: O God, put forth thy strength: / stablish the thing, O God, that thou hast wrought for us.
verses.26: For thy temple’s sake at Jerusalem / kings shall bring presents unto thee.
verses.27: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, trampling under foot the pieces of silver; / scatter thou the peoples that delight in war.
verses.28: Then shall the princes come out of Egypt; / Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God.
verses.29: Sing unto God, O ye kingdoms of the earth:/ O sing praises unto the Lord;
verses.30: Who rideth in the high heavens, which are of old: / lo, he doth send out his voice, yea, and that a mighty voice.
verses.31: Ascribe ye the power to God; his majesty is over Israel, / and his strength is in the clouds.
verses.32: O God, terrible art thou in thy holy places: / even the God of Israel; he giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.

verses.1: Save me, O God; / for the waters are come in, even unto my soul.
verses.2: I stick fast in the deep mire, where no ground is: / I am come into deep waters, so that the floods run over me.
verses.3: I am weary of crying; my throat is dry: / my sight faileth me for waiting so long upon my God.
verses.4: They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head: / they that are mine enemies, and would destroy me guiltless, are mighty.
verses.5: I paid them the things that I never took: / God, thou knowest my foolishness, and my faults are not hid from thee.
verses.6: Let not them that trust in thee be ashamed for my cause, O Lord GOD of hosts: / let not those that seek thee be confounded through me, O God of Israel.
verses.7: And why? for thy sake I have suffered reproach: / shame hath covered my face.
verses.8: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, / even an alien unto my mother’s children.
verses.9: For the zeal of thine house hath even eaten me; / and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
verses.10: I wept, and chastened myself with fasting, / and that was turned to my reproach.
verses.11: I put on sackcloth also, / and they jested upon me.
verses.12: They that sit in the gate talk about me, / and the drunkards make songs upon me.
verses.13: But, LORD, I make my prayer unto thee / in an acceptable time.
verses.14: Hear me, O God, in the multitude of thy mercy, / even in the truth of thy salvation.
verses.15: Take me out of the mire, that I sink not; / O let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
verses.16: Let not the water-flood drown me, neither let the deep swallow me up, / and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
verses.17: Hear me, O LORD, for thy loving-kindness is comfortable: / turn thee unto me according to the multitude of thy mercies.
verses.18: And hide not thy face from thy servant; / for I am in trouble: O haste thee, and hear me.
verses.19: Draw nigh unto my soul, and save it: / O deliver me, because of mine enemies.
verses.20: Thou knowest my reproach, my shame, and my dishonour: / mine adversaries are all in thy sight.
verses.21: Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness: / I looked for some to have pity on me, but there was no man, neither found I any to comfort me.
verses.22: They gave me gaff to eat; / and when I was thirsty they gave me vinegar to drink.
verses.23: But as for me, when I am poor and in heaviness, / thy help, O God, shall lift me up.
verses.24: I will praise the Name of God with a song, / and magnify him with thanksgiving.
verses.25: This also shall please the LORD better than an ox, / or a bullock that hath horns and hoofs.
verses.26: The humble shall consider this, and be glad: / seek ye after God, and your soul shall live.
verses.27: For the LORD heareth the poor, / and despiseth not his prisoners.
verses.28: Let heaven and earth praise him, / the sea, and all that moveth therein.
verses.29: For God will save Sion, and build the cities of Judah, / that men may dwell there, and have it in possession.
verses.30: The posterity also of his servants shall inherit it; / and they that love his Name shall dwell therein.

verses.1: O God, make speed to save me; / O LORD, make haste to help me.
verses.2: Let them be ashamed and confounded that seek after my soul; / let them be turned backward and put to confusion that wish me evil.
verses.3: Let them for their reward be soon brought to shame / that cry over me, ‘There, there.’
verses.4: But let those that seek thee be joyful and glad in thee; / and let all such as love thy salvation say alway, ‘The LORD be praised.’
verses.5: As for me, I am poor and in misery; / haste thee unto me, O God.
verses.6: Thou art my helper and my redeemer; / O LORD, make no long tarrying.

verses.1: In thee O LORD have I put my trust; / let me never be put to confusion.
verses.2: Deliver me and rescue me in thy righteousness: / incline thine ear unto me and save me.
verses.3: Be thou my stronghold, whereunto I may alway resort; / thou hast promised to help me, for thou art my rock and my castle.
verses.4: Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the ungodly, / out of the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
verses.5: For thou, O Lord, art the thing that I long for: / thou, LORD, art my trust, even from my youth.
verses.6: Through thee have I been holden up ever since I was born: / thou art he that took me out of my mother’s womb; my praise shall be always of thee.
verses.7: I am become as it were a wonder unto many, / but my sure trust is in thee.
verses.8: O let my mouth be filled with thy praise, / and with thy glory all the day long.
verses.9: Cast me not away in the time of age: / forsake me not when my strength faileth me.
verses.10: For mine enemies speak concerning me; / and they that watch for my soul take their counsel together,
verses.11: Saying, ‘God hath forsaken him; / pursue him and take him, for there is none to deliver him.’
verses.12: Go not far from me, O God: / O my God, haste thee to help me.
verses.13: Let them be confounded and perish that are against my soul: / let them be covered with shame and dishonour that seek to do me evil.
verses.14: As for me, I will patiently abide alway, / and will praise thee more and more.
verses.15: My mouth shall tell of thy righteousness, and of thy salvation all the day long; / for I know no end thereof.
verses.16: I will go forth in the strength of the Lord GOD, / and will make mention of thy righteousness only.
verses.17: Thou, O God, hast taught me from my youth, / and even until now do I tell of thy wondrous works.
verses.18: Forsake me not, O God, in mine old age, when I am gray-headed, / until I have showed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to all them that are yet for to come.
verses.19: Thy righteousness, O God, is very high, / and great things are they that thou hast done; O God, who is like unto thee?
verses.20: How many and sore troubles hast thou showed me! yet wilt thou turn and refresh me: / yea, thou wilt bring me up from the depths of the earth again.
verses.21: Thou wilt bring me to great honour, / and turn again and comfort me.
verses.22: I also will praise thee and thy faithfulness, O God, playing upon an instrument of music: / unto thee will I sing upon the harp, O thou Holy One of Israel.
verses.23: My lips will rejoice when I sing unto thee: / and so will my soul whom thou hast delivered.
verses.24: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long; / for they are confounded and brought to shame that seek to do me evil.

verses.1: Give the king thy judgements, O God, / and thy righteousness unto the king’s son.
verses.2: Then shall he judge thy people according unto right, / and thy poor with justice.
verses.3: The mountains also shall bring peace, / and the little hills righteousness unto the people.
verses.4: He shall keep the simple folk by their right, / save the children of the poor, and punish the wrong doer.
verses.5: He shall live as long as the sun, / and while the moon endureth, from one generation to another.
verses.6: He shall come down like the rain upon the mown grass, / even as the showers that water the earth.
verses.7: In his time shall righteousness flourish; / yea, and abundance of peace, so long as the moon endureth.
verses.8: Let his dominion also be from sea to sea, / and from the River unto the world’s end.
verses.9: Let them that dwell in the wilderness kneel before him; / and let his enemies lick the dust.
verses.10: Let the kings of Tarshish and of the isles give presents, / and the kings of Arabia and Seba bring gifts.
verses.11: Let all kings fall down before him, / and all nations do him service.
verses.12: For he shall deliver the poor when he crieth; / the needy also, and him that hath no helper.
verses.13: He shall have pity on the weak and the needy, / and shall preserve the souls of the poor.
verses.14: He shall deliver their souls from falsehood and wrong; / and dear shall their blood be in his sight.
verses.15: So let him live, and unto him let there be given of the gold of Arabia; / let prayer be made for him continually, and all day long let him be praised.
verses.16: Let there be an abundance of grain in the land, / even upon the top of the mountains.
verses.17: Let its fruit wave like Lebanon, / and let men flourish out of the city like grass upon the earth.
verses.18: Let his name endure for ever; / let his name continue as long as the sun.
verses.19: Let all the tribes of the earth be blessed through him, / and let all nations call him happy.
verses.20: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who only doeth wondrous things;
verses.21: And blessed be the Name of his majesty for ever: / and let all the earth be filled with his majesty. Amen and Amen.

verses.1: Truly God is loving unto Israel: / even unto such as are of a clean heart.
verses.2: Nevertheless, my feet were almost gone; / my treadings had well-nigh slipt.
verses.3: And why? I was grieved at the wicked: I do also see the ungodly in such prosperity.
verses.4: For they have no torments, / but are lusty and strong.
verses.5: They come in no misfortune like other folk; / neither are they plagued like other men.
verses.6: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck, / and violence covereth them as a garment.
verses.7: Their iniquity cometh forth from the heart, / and the imaginations of their mind overflow.
verses.8: They scoff and speak of evil, / and talk proudly of oppression.
verses.9: They stretch forth their mouth unto the heavens, / and their tongue goeth through the world.
verses.10: Therefore turn the people unto them, / and find no fault in them.
verses.11: ‘Tush,’ say they, ‘how should God perceive it? / is there knowledge in the Most High?’
verses.12: Lo, these are the ungodly; / they are alway at ease, and get riches in possession.
verses.13: Then surely in vain have I cleansed my heart, / and washed my hands in innocency.
verses.14: For all the day long have I been punished, / and chastened every morning.
verses.15: If I had said, ‘I will speak thus’, / lo, then I should have condemned the generation of thy children.
verses.16: Then thought I to understand this, / but it was too hard for me,
verses.17: Until I went into the sanctuary of God, / and considered the end of these men;
verses.18: For surely thou dost set them in slippery places, / and castest them down, and destroyest them.
verses.19: Oh, how suddenly do they consume, / perish, and come to a fearful end!
verses.20: Yea, even like as a dream when one awaketh, / so, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image.
verses.21: Thus my soul was grieved, / and my heart within me was stricken.
verses.22: So foolish was I, and ignorant, / even as it were a beast before thee.
verses.23: Nevertheless, I am alway by thee; / for thou hast holden me by my right hand.
verses.24: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, / and after that receive me with glory.
verses.25: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire in comparison of thee.
verses.26: My flesh and my heart faileth; / but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
verses.27: For lo, they that forsake thee shall perish: / thou destroyest all them that are unfaithful unto thee.
verses.28: But it is good for me to hold me fast by God, to put my trust in the Lord GOD, / and to speak of all thy works in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

verses.1: O God, wherefore hast thou cast us off for ever? / why is thy wrath so hot against the sheep of thy pasture?
verses.2: O think upon thy congregation, / which thou hast purchased of old;
verses.3: Which thou hast redeemed to be the tribe of thine inheritance: / think upon mount Sion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
verses.4: Direct thy steps unto the perpetual ruins: / all the evil that the enemy hath done in the sanctuary.
verses.5: Thine adversaries roar in the midst of thy congregation, / and set up their banners for tokens.
verses.6: They seem like men that lift up axes upon a grove of trees; / for now they break down all the carved work thereof with axes and hammers.
verses.7: They have set thy sanctuary on fire, / and have defiled the dwelling-place of thy Name, even unto the ground.
verses.8: Yea, they said in their hearts, ‘Let us make havoc of them altogether’: / thus have they burnt up all the houses of God in the land.
verses.9: We see not our tokens; there is no more any prophet: / no, not one is there among us that knoweth how long.
verses.10: O God, how long shall the adversary do this dishonour? / shall the enemy blaspheme thy Name for ever?
verses.11: Why dost thou draw back thy hand, / and keep thy right hand in thy bosom?
verses.12: Yet God is my King of old: / the help that is done upon earth, he doeth it himself.
verses.13: Thou didst divide the sea through thy power:/ thou didst break the heads of the dragons in the waters.
verses.14: Thou didst crush the heads of Leviathan, / and gavest him to be food for the creatures of the wilderness.
verses.15: Thou didst cleave open fountain and flood: / thou driedst up ever-flowing streams.
verses.16: The day is thine, and the night is thine: / thou hast prepared the light and the sun.
verses.17: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: / thou hast made summer and winter.
verses.18: Remember this, O LORD, how the enemy hath reproached, / and how a foolish people hath blasphemed thy Name.
verses.19: O deliver not the soul of thy turtle-dove unto the wild beast: / and forget not the life of thy poor for ever.
verses.20: Look upon the covenant; / for the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty.
verses.21: O let not the oppressed go away ashamed; / but let the poor and needy give praise unto thy Name.
verses.22: Arise, O God, maintain thine own cause: / remember how the foolish man blasphemeth thee all the day long.
verses.23: Forget not the voice of thine enemies: / the tumult of them that hate thee increaseth ever more and more.

verses.1: Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks; / yea, unto thee do we give thanks.
verses.2: Thy Name also is so nigh; / and that do thy wondrous works declare.
verses.3: When I reach the appointed time, / I shall judge according unto right.
verses.4: Though the earth be dissolved, and all the inhabiters thereof, / I bear up the pillars of it.
verses.5: I said unto the fools, ‘Deal not so madly’, / and to the ungodly, ‘Set not up your horn’.
verses.6: Set not up your horn on high, / and speak not with a stiff neck.
verses.7: For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, / nor yet from the south.
verses.8: And why? God is the judge; / he putteth down one, and setteth up another.
verses.9: For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, and the wine is red; / it is full mixed, and he poureth out of the same.
verses.10: As for the dregs thereof, / all the ungodly of the earth shall drink them, and suck them out.
verses.11: But I will talk of the God of Jacob, / and praise him for ever.
verses.12: All the horns of the ungodly also will I break, / but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.

verses.1: In Judah is God known: / his Name is great in Israel.
verses.2: At Salem is his tabernacle, / and his dwelling in Sion.
verses.3: There brake he the arrows of the bow, / the shield, the sword, and the battle.
verses.4: Glorious art thou, and more majestic / than the everlasting hills.
verses.5: The stout of heart are spoiled, they have slept their sleep; / and the hands of all the men of might have failed.
verses.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, / both the chariot and horse are fallen.
verses.7: Thou, even thou art to be feared; / and who may stand in thy sight when thou art angry?
verses.8: Thou didst cause thy judgement to be heard from heaven; / the earth trembled and was still,
verses.9: When God arose to judgement, / and to help all the meek upon earth.
verses.10: The wrath of man shall turn to thy praise; / and the remainder of wrath shall honour thee.
verses.11: Promise unto the LORD your God, and keep it; / let all that are round about him bring gifts, even unto him that ought to be feared.
verses.12: He shall cut off the spirit of princes, / and is terrible unto the kings of the earth.

verses.1: I Will cry unto God with my voice: / even unto God will I cry with my voice, and he shall hearken unto me.
verses.2: In the time of my trouble I sought the Lord: / in the night my hand was stretched out without ceasing; my soul refused comfort.
verses.3: When I think upon God, I am in heaviness: / when I meditate, my spirit fainteth.
verses.4: Thou holdest mine eyelids from closing: / I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
verses.5: I Have considered the days of old, / and called to mind the years that are long past.
verses.6: I commune with my heart in the night: / I meditate and search my spirit.
verses.7: Will the Lord cast us off for ever? / and will he be no more entreated?
verses.8: Is his mercy clean gone for ever? / and is his promise come utterly to an end for evermore?
verses.9: Hath God forgotten to be gracious? / and hath he shut up his loving-kindness in displeasure?
verses.10: And I said, ‘It is mine own infirmity: / but I will remember the years of the right hand of the Most High.’
verses.11: I will remember the works of the LORD, / and call to mind thy wonders of old time.
verses.12: I will think also of all thy works, / and meditate upon thy doings.
verses.13: Thy way, O God, is holy: / who is so great a God as our God?
verses.14: Thou art the God that doest wonders, / and didst declare thy power among the peoples.
verses.15: Thou didst mightily deliver thy people, / even the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
verses.16: The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee, and were afraid: / the depths also were troubled.
verses.17: The clouds poured out water, the skies thundered, / and thine arrows went abroad.
verses.18: The voice of thy thunder was in the whirlwind; / thy lightnings lit up the world; the earth was moved, and shook withal.
verses.19: Thy way was in the sea, and thy paths in the great waters, / and yet thy footsteps were not known.
verses.20: Thou leddest thy people like sheep, / by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

verses.1: Hear my teaching, O my people: / incline your ears unto the words of my mouth.
verses.2: I will open my mouth in a parable; / I will utter dark sayings from of old;
verses.3: Which we have heard and known, / and such as our fathers have told us.
verses.4: We will not hide them from their children, but tell them to the generation to come, / even the praises of the LORD, and his might, and his wonderful works that he hath done.
verses.5: He made a covenant with Jacob, and gave Israel a law, / which he commanded our forefathers to teach their children;
verses.6: That the next generation might know it, / and the children which were yet unborn;
verses.7: To the intent that when they rose up, / they might show their children the same;
verses.8: That they might put their trust in God, / and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments;
verses.9: And not be as their forefathers, a faithless and stubborn generation, / a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not faithful to God;
verses.10: Like as the children of Ephraim, who being armed, and carrying bows, / turned themselves back in the day of battle.
verses.11: They kept not the covenant of God, / and would not walk in his law;
verses.12: But forgat what he had done, / and the wonderful works that he had showed for them.
verses.13: Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, / in the land of Egypt, even in the field of Zoan.
verses.14: He divided the sea, and let them go through; / and he made the waters to stand as a heap.
verses.15: In the day-time also he led them with a cloud, / and all the night through with a light of fire.
verses.16: A He rent the hard rocks in the wilderness, / and gave them drink abundantly as from the deep.
verses.17: He brought water out of the stony rock, / so that it gushed out like the rivers.
verses.18: Yet for all this they sinned more against him, / and provoked the Most High in the wilderness.
verses.19: They tempted God in their hearts, / demanding the food which they craved.
verses.20: They spake against God also, saying, / ‘Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
verses.21: He smote the stony rock indeed, that the waters gushed out, and the streams flowed withal; / but can he give bread also, or provide flesh for his people?’
verses.22: When the LORD heard this, he was wroth; / so the fire was kindled in Jacob, and there came up heavy displeasure against Israel;
verses.23: Because they believed not in God, / and put not their trust in his help.
verses.24: Yet he commanded the clouds above, / and opened the doors of heaven.
verses.25: He rained down manna also upon them for to eat, / and gave them food from heaven.
verses.26: So man did eat angels’ bread; / for he sent them food enough.
verses.27: He caused the east wind to blow in the heavens; / and through his power he brought in the south-west wind.
verses.28: He rained flesh upon them as thick as dust, / and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.
verses.29: He let it fall among their tents, / even round about their habitations.
verses.30: So they did eat and were well filled; / for he gave them their own desire.
verses.31: But before they had satisfied their craving, and while the food was yet in their mouths, / the heavy wrath of God came upon them,
verses.32: And he slew the strongest of them, / and smote down the chosen men that were in Israel.
verses.33: But for all this they sinned yet more, / and believed not his wondrous works.
verses.34: Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, / and their years in terror.
verses.35: When he slew them, they sought him, / and turned them back, and inquired earnestly after God.
verses.36: And they remembered that God was their strength, / and that God Most High was their redeemer.
verses.37: Nevertheless, they did but flatter him with their mouth, / and dissembled with him in their tongue.
verses.38: For their heart was not stedfast with him, / neither continued they faithful in his covenant.
verses.39: But he was so merciful, that he forgave their misdeeds, / and destroyed them not.
verses.40: Yea, many a time turned he his wrath away, / and would not suffer his whole displeasure to arise.
verses.41: For he considered that they were but flesh, / and that they were even a wind that passeth away, and cometh not again.
verses.42: Many a time did God’s people rebel against him in the wilderness, / and grieve him in the desert.
verses.43: They turned back and tempted God, / and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
verses.44: They thought not of his hand, / and of the day when he delivered them from the hand of the enemy;
verses.45: How he had wrought his miracles in Egypt, / and his wonders in the field of Zoan.
verses.46: He turned their rivers into blood, / so that they could not drink of their streams.
verses.47: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them, / and frogs, which destroyed them.
verses.48: He gave their fruit unto the caterpillar, / and their labour unto the locust.
verses.49: He destroyed their vines with hail-stones, / and their sycamore-trees with the frost.
verses.50: He smote their cattle also with hail-stones, / and their flocks with hot thunderbolts.
verses.51: He cast upon them the fury of his wrath, anger, displeasure, and trouble: / a band of destroying angels.
verses.52: He made a way for his indignation, and spared not their soul from death, / but gave their life over to the pestilence;
verses.53: And smote all the first-born in Egypt, / the firstlings of their strength in the dwellings of Ham.
verses.54: But as for his own people, he led them forth like sheep, / and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
verses.55: He brought them out safely, that they did not fear, / and overwhelmed their enemies in the sea.
verses.56: He brought them unto his holy border, / even to the mountain which he had purchased with his right hand.
verses.57: He cast out the nations also before them, / caused their land to be divided among them for an heritage, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
verses.58: Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, / and kept not his testimonies;
verses.59: But turned back, and fell away like their forefathers, / starting aside like a broken bow.
verses.60: For they grieved him with their hill-altars, / and provoked him to displeasure with their images.
verses.61: When God heard this, he was wroth, / and took sore displeasure at Israel;
verses.62: So that he forsook the tabernacle in Shiloh, / even the tent that he had pitched among men.
verses.63: He delivered his strength into captivity, / and his glory into the enemy’s hand.
verses.64: He gave his people over also unto the sword, / and was wroth with his inheritance.
verses.65: The fire consumed their young men, / and their maidens were not given to marriage.
verses.66: Their priests were slain with the sword; / and their widows made no lamentation.
verses.67: So the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, / and like a giant refreshed with wine.
verses.68: He smote his enemies backward, / and put them to a perpetual shame.
verses.69: He refused the tabernacle of Joseph, / and chose not the tribe of Ephraim;
verses.70: But chose the tribe of Judah, / even the hill of Sion which he loved.
verses.71: And he built his sanctuary like the heights of heaven, / and like the earth which he hath founded for ever.
verses.72: He chose David also his servant, / and took him away from the sheep-folds.
verses.73: As he was following the ewes with their young he brought him, / that he might feed Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.
verses.74: So he fed them with a faithful and true heart, / and ruled them prudently with all his power.

verses.1: O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; / thy holy temple have they defiled, and made Jerusalem a heap of stones.
verses.2: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, / and the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
verses.3: Their blood have they shed like water on every side of Jerusalem; / and there was no man to bury them.
verses.4: We are become an open shame to our neighbours, / a very scorn and derision unto them that are round about us.
verses.5: LORD, how long wilt thou be angry? / shall thy jealousy burn like fire for ever?
verses.6: Pour out thine indignation upon the nations that have not known thee, / and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy Name.
verses.7: For they have devoured Jacob, / and laid waste his dwelling-place.
verses.8: O remember not against us the offences of our forefathers, but have mercy upon us, and that soon; / for we are come to great misery.
verses.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy Name; / O deliver us, and be merciful unto our sins, for thy Name’s sake.
verses.10: Wherefore should the nations say, / ‘Where is now their God?’
verses.11: O let the vengeance of thy servants’ blood that is shed / be openly showed upon the nations in our sight.
verses.12: O let the sorrowful sighing of the prisoners come before thee; / according to the greatness of thy power, preserve thou those that are appointed to die.
verses.13: And for the blasphemy wherewith our neighbours have blasphemed thee, / reward thou them, O Lord, seven-fold into their bosom.
verses.14: So we, that are thy people and the sheep of thy pasture, shall give thee thanks for ever, / and will be showing forth thy praise from generation to generation.

verses.1: Hear O thou Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; / show thyself also, thou that sittest upon the cherubim.
verses.2: Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, / stir up thy strength, and come and help us.
verses.3: Turn us again, O God; / show the light of thy countenance, and we shall be whole.
verses.4: O Lord God of hosts, / how long wilt thou be angry with thy people that prayeth?
verses.5: Thou hast fed them with the bread of tears, / and hast given them plenteousness of tears to drink.
verses.6: Thou makest us a very strife unto our neighbours, / and our enemies laugh us to scorn.
verses.7: Turn us again, O God of hosts; / show the light of thy countenance, and we shall be whole.
verses.8: Thou broughtest a vine out of Egypt; / thou didst drive out the nations, and plant it in.
verses.9: Thou madest room for it; / and when it had taken root it filled the land.
verses.10: The hills were covered with the shadow of it, / and the mighty cedars with the boughs thereof.
verses.11: She stretched out her branches unto the sea, / and her boughs unto the River.
verses.12: Why hast thou then broken down her fences, / so that all they that go by pluck her grapes?
verses.13: The wild boar out of the wood doth root it up, / and the wild beasts of the field devour it.
verses.14: Turn us again, O God of hosts; / show the light of thy countenance, and we shall be whole.
verses.15: Look down from heaven, behold, and visit this vine, and the stock that thy right hand hath planted, / and the branch that thou madest so strong for thyself.
verses.16: It is burnt with fire and cut down; / they perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
verses.17: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand, / and upon the son of man, whom thou madest so strong for thine own self.
verses.18: And so shall we not go back from thee: / O let us live, and we will call upon thy Name.
verses.19: Turn us again, O LORD God of hosts; / show the light of thy countenance, and we shall be whole.

verses.1: O Sing merrily unto God our strength; / make a cheerful noise unto the God of Jacob.
verses.2: Raise the psalm and sound the timbrel, / the merry harp with the lute.
verses.3: Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, / at the full moon, for our solemn feast day.
verses.4: For this was made a statute for Israel, / and a law of the God of Jacob.
verses.5: This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony, / when he went forth against the land of Egypt.
verses.6: I Heard the voice of one that I knew not: / ‘I eased his shoulder from the burden, and his hands were freed from the load.
verses.7: Thou didst call in trouble, and I delivered thee; / I heard thee in the thunder-cloud; I proved thee also at the Waters of Strife.
verses.8: Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: / O Israel, if thou wouldest hearken unto me!
verses.9: There shall no strange god be in thee, / neither shalt thou worship any other god.
verses.10: I am the LORD thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: / open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.11: But my people would not hear my voice; / and Israel would not obey me.
verses.12: So I gave them up unto their stubborn hearts, / and let them follow their own imaginations.
verses.13: O that my people would hearken unto me, / that Israel would walk in my ways!
verses.14: I should soon put down their enemies, / and turn my hand against their adversaries.
verses.15: The haters ofthe LORD should feign obedience unto him; / but their time should endure for ever.
verses.16: I would feed them also with the finest wheatflour; / and with honey out of the stony rock would I satisfy thee.’

verses.1: God standeth in the divine assembly; / in the midst of the gods he judgeth:
verses.2: ‘How long will ye give wrong judgement, / and accept the persons of the ungodly?
verses.3: Do justice for the poor and the fatherless; / see that such as are in need and necessity have right.
verses.4: Deliver the outcast and poor; / save them from the hand of the ungodly.’
verses.5: They have neither knowledge nor understanding; they walk on still in darkness; / all the foundations of the earth are out of course.
verses.6: I have said, ‘Ye are gods, / and ye are all the children of the Most High.
verses.7: But ye shall die like men, / and fall like one of the princes.’
verses.8: Arise, O God, and judge thou the earth; / for thou shalt take all nations to thine inheritance.

verses.1: O God, keep not still silence: / hold not thy peace, and be not quiet, O God.
verses.2: For lo, thine enemies make a murmuring; / and they that hate thee have lift up their head.
verses.3: They have imagined craftily against thy people, / and taken counsel against thy secret ones.
verses.4: They have said, ‘Come, and let us root them out, that they be no more a people, / and that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.’
verses.5: For they have cast their heads together with one consent, / and are confederate against thee:
verses.6: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, / of Moab and the Hagarenes,
verses.7: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, / the Philistines with them that dwell at Tyre.
verses.8: Assyria also is joined with them; / and they have helped the children of Lot.
verses.9: But do thou to them as unto the Midianites; / as unto Sisera and unto Jabin at the river Kishon;
verses.10: Who perished at En-dor, / and became as the dung of the earth.
verses.11: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb; / yea, make all their princes like as Zebah and Zalmunna;
verses.12: Who have said, ‘ Let us take to ourselves / the pastures of God in possession.’
verses.13: O my God, make them like unto the whirling dust, / and as the chaff before the wind;
verses.14: Like as the fire that burneth up the forest, / and as the flame that setteth the mountains ablaze;
verses.15: Pursue them even so with thy tempest, / and make them afraid with thy storm.
verses.16: Make their faces ashamed, / that they may seek thy Name, O LORD.
verses.17: Let them be confounded and dismayed for ever; / let them be put to shame and perish.
verses.18: And let them know that thou, even thou only, whose Name is the LORD, / art the Most High over all the earth.

verses.1: O How lovely are thy dwellings, / thou LORD of hosts!
verses.2: My soul hath a desire and longing to enter into the courts of the LORD:/ my heart and my flesh rejoice in the living God.
verses.3: Yea, the sparrow hath found her an house, and the swallow a nest where she may lay her young: / even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King and my God.
verses.4: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house; / they will be alway praising thee.
verses.5: Blessed are the men whose strength is in thee, / in whose heart are the pilgrim ways;
verses.6: Who going through the Vale of Misery use it for a well; / yea, the early rain covereth it with blessings.
verses.7: They go from strength to strength, / and unto the God of gods appeareth every one of them in Sion.
verses.8: O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: / hearken, O God of Jacob.
verses.9: Behold, O God, our shield, / and look upon the face of thine anointed.
verses.10: For one day in thy courts / is better than a thousand.
verses.11: Had rather be a door-keeper in the house of my God, / than to dwell in the tents of ungodliness.
verses.12: For the LORD God is a light and defence; the LORD will give grace and glory; / and no good thing shall he withhold from them that lead a godly life.
verses.13: O Lord God of hosts, / blessed is the man that putteth his trust in thee.

verses.1: Lord, thou art become gracious unto thy land: / thou hast restored the fortunes of Jacob.
verses.2: Thou hast forgiven the offence of thy people, / and covered all their sin.
verses.3: Thou hast taken away all thy displeasure, / and turned thyself from thy wrathful indignation.
verses.4: Turn us, O God our Saviour, / and let thine anger cease from us.
verses.5: Wilt thou be displeased at us for ever? / and wilt thou stretch out thy wrath from one generation to another?
verses.6: Wilt thou not turn again and quicken us, / that thy people may rejoice in thee?
verses.7: O Lord, show thy mercy upon us, / and grant us thy salvation.
verses.8: I Will hearken what the LORD God will say: / for he shall speak peace unto his people and to his saints, / and unto them that turn their heart to him.
verses.9: Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him, / that glory may dwell in our land.
verses.10: Mercy and truth are met together: / righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
verses.11: Truth springeth out of the earth; / and righteousness hath looked down from heaven.
verses.12: Yea, the LORD shall give what is good; / and our land shall yield her increase.
verses.13: Righteousness shall go before him, / and shall direct his going in the way.

verses.1: Bow down thine ear, O LORD, and hear me; / for I am poor and needy.
verses.2: Preserve thou my soul, for I am godly: / save thy servant that putteth his trust in thee.
verses.3: Thou art my God; be merciful unto me, O Lord; / for all the day long do I call upon thee.
verses.4: Comfort the soul of thy servant; / for unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.
verses.5: For thou, Lord, art good and gracious, / and of great mercy unto all them that call upon thee.
verses.6: Give ear, LORD, unto my prayer, / and ponder the voice of my humble desires.
verses.7: In the time of my trouble I will call upon thee; / for thou hearest me.
verses.8: Among the gods there is none like unto thee, O Lord; / there is not one that can do as thou doest.
verses.9: All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship thee, O Lord, / and shall glorify thy Name.
verses.10: For thou art great and doest wondrous things: / thou art God alone.
verses.11: Teach me thy way, O LORD, and I will walk in thy truth: / O knit my heart unto thee, that I may fear thy Name.
verses.12: I will thank thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart, / and will praise thy Name for evermore.
verses.13: For great is thy mercy toward me; / and thou hast delivered my soul from the nethermost hell.
verses.14: O God, the proud are risen against me, / and a band of violent men have sought after my soul, and have not set thee before their eyes.
verses.15: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, / long-suffering, plenteous in mercy and truth.
verses.16: O turn thee then unto me, and have mercy upon me; / give thy strength unto thy servant, and help the son of thy handmaid.
verses.17: Show some token upon me for good, that they who hate me may see it and be ashamed, / because thou, LORD, hast helped me, and comforted me.

verses.1: His foundation is upon the holy hills: / the LORD loveth the gates of Sion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
verses.2: Very excellent things are spoken of thee, / thou city of God.
verses.3: I Will make mention of Rahab and Babylon, / as among them that know me.
verses.4: Behold Philistia and Tyre, with Ethiopia; / lo, this one was born there.
verses.5: Yea, of Sion it shall be said, ‘This one and that one were born in her’; / and the Most High himself shall establish her.
verses.6: The LORD shall reckon when he writeth up the peoples, / that this one was born there.
verses.7: The singers also and dancers shall say, / ‘All my fresh springs are in thee.’

verses.1: O Lord God of my salvation, / I have cried day and night before thee.
verses.2: O let my prayer enter into thy presence: / incline thine ear unto my calling.
verses.3: For my soul is full of troubles, / and my life draweth nigh unto the grave.
verses.4: I am counted as one of them that go down into the pit; / I am even as a man that hath no strength;
verses.5: Like one cast forth among the dead, like the slain that lie in the grave, / whom thou rememberest no more, and they are cut off from thy hand.
verses.6: Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, / in places of darkness, and in the deeps.
verses.7: Thine indignation lieth hard upon me, / and thou hast vexed me with all thy storms.
verses.8: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me, / and hast made me to be abhorred of them.
verses.9: I am so fast in prison that I cannot get forth; / my sight faileth for very trouble.
verses.10: LORD I have called daily upon thee: / I have stretched forth my hands unto thee.
verses.11: Dost thou show wonders for the dead? / or shall the dead rise up and praise thee?
verses.12: Shall thy loving-kindness be declared in the grave, / or thy faithfulness in Destruction?
verses.13: Shall thy wondrous works be known in the dark, / and thy righteousness in the land where all things are forgotten?
verses.14: Unto thee have I cried, O LORD;/ and early shall my prayer come before thee.
verses.15: LORD, why abhorrest thou my soul, / and hidest thou thy face from me?
verses.16: From my youth up I am in misery and ready to die; / thy terrors have I suffered with a troubled mind.
verses.17: Thy wrathful displeasure goeth over me, / and the fear of thee hath undone me.
verses.18: They came round about me like water all the day long, / and compassed me together on every side.
verses.19: My lovers and friends hast thou put away from me, / and hid mine acquaintance out of my sight.

verses.1: My song shall be alway of the loving-kindness of the LORD; / with my mouth will I ever be showing thy faithfulness from one generation to another.
verses.2: For I have said, ‘Loving-kindness shall be built up for ever; / thy faithfulness shalt thou stablish in the heavens.’
verses.3: ‘I HAVE made a covenant with my chosen: / I have sworn unto David my servant;
verses.4: Thy seed will I stablish for ever, / and set up thy throne from one generation to another.’
verses.5: O Lord, the very heavens shall praise thy wondrous works, / and thy faithfulness in the congregation of the holy ones.
verses.6: For who is he in the skies that shall be compared unto the LORD? / and what is he among the gods that shall be like unto the LORD?
verses.7: God is very greatly to be feared in the council of the holy ones, / and to be had in reverence above all them that are round about him.
verses.8: O Lord God of hosts, who is like unto thee? / thy faithfulness, most mighty LORD, is on every side.
verses.9: Thou rulest the raging of the sea; / thou stillest the waves thereof when they arise.
verses.10: Thou didst crush Rahab as one that is pierced; / thou didst scatter thine enemies abroad with thy mighty arm.
verses.11: The heavens are thine, / the earth also is thine: / thou hast laid the foundation of the round world, and all that is therein.
verses.12: Thou hast made the north and the south: / Tabor and Hermon rejoice in thy Name.
verses.13: Thou hast a mighty arm: / strong is thy hand, and high is thy right hand.
verses.14: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of thy throne: / mercy and truth go before thy face.
verses.15: Blessed is the people that can rejoice in thee: / they shall walk, O LORD, in the light of thy countenance.
verses.16: Their delight shall be in thy Name all the day long; / and in thy righteousness shall they be exalted.
verses.17: For thou art the glory of their strength, / and by thy favour our horn is exalted.
verses.18: For to the LORD belongeth our shield, / and our king to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.19: Thou spakest sometime in a vision unto thy saints, and saidst, / ‘I have laid help upon one that is mighty; I have exalted one chosen out of the people.
verses.20: I have found David my servant: / with my holy oil have I anointed him.
verses.21: My hand shall hold him fast, / and my arm shall strengthen him.
verses.22: The enemy shall not be able to do him violence: / the son of wickedness shall not hurt him.
verses.23: I will beat down his foes before his face, / and smite them that hate him.
verses.24: My faithfulness also and my mercy shall be with him: / and in my Name shall his horn be exalted.
verses.25: I will set his hand also on the sea, / and his right hand on the rivers.
verses.26: He shall call me, “Thou art my Father, / my God, and the rock of my salvation.”
verses.27: And I will make him my first-born, / the highest of the kings of the earth.
verses.28: My mercy will I keep for him for evermore; / and my covenant shall stand fast with him.
verses.29: His seed also will I make to endure for ever, / and his throne as the days of heaven.
verses.30: But if his children forsake my law, / and walk not in my judgements;
verses.31: If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandments, / I will visit their offences with the rod, and their sin with scourges.
verses.32: Nevertheless, my loving-kindness will I not utterly take from him, / nor suffer my faithfulness to fail.
verses.33: My covenant will I not break, / nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips.
verses.34: Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; / I will not lie unto David;
verses.35: His seed shall endure for ever, / and his throne is like as the sun before me.
verses.36: It shall stand fast for evermore as the moon, / and as the faithful witness in the sky.’
verses.37: But thou hast abhorred and forsaken thine anointed, / and art displeased at him.
verses.38: Thou hast broken the covenant with thy servant, / and cast his crown to the ground.
verses.39: Thou hast overthrown all his fences, / and broken down his strongholds.
verses.40: All they that go by spoil him, / and he is become a reproach to his neighbours.
verses.41: Thou hast set up the right hand of his adversaries, / and made all his enemies to rejoice.
verses.42: Thou hast turned back the edge of his sword, / and givest him not victory in the battle.
verses.43: Thou hast put out his glory, / and cast his throne down to the ground.
verses.44: The days of his youth hast thou shortened, / and covered him with dishonour.
verses.45: How long, O LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever? / how long shall thy wrath burn like fire?
verses.46: O remember how short my time is; / wherefore hast thou made all men for nought?
verses.47: What man is he that shall live on, and not see death? / and shall he deliver his soul from the power of the grave?
verses.48: Where are thy former loving-kindnesses, O Lord, / which thou swarest unto David in thy faithfulness?
verses.49: Remember, Lord, the reproach that thy servants have, / and how I do bear in my bosom the insults of the peoples;
verses.50: Wherewith thine enemies have reproached, O LORD, / wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of thine anointed.
verses.51: Praised be the LORD for evermore. / Amen and Amen.

verses.1: Lord, thou hast been our refuge, / from one generation to another.
verses.2: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever the earth and the world were made, / thou art God from everlasting, and world without end.
verses.3: Thou turnest man back to the dust, / and thou sayest, “Return, ye children of men.’
verses.4: For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, / and as a watch in the night.
verses.5: Thou carriest them away as with a flood, and they are even as a sleep; / in the morning they are like grass that groweth up.
verses.6: In the morning it is green and groweth up, / but in the evening it is cut down and withered.
verses.7: For we consume away in thy displeasure, / and are afraid at thy wrathful indignation.
verses.8: Thou hast set our misdeeds before thee, / and our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.
verses.9: For when thou art angry all our days are gone: / we bring our years to an end, as it were a tale that is told.
verses.10: The days of our age are threescore years and ten, / or, if men be so strong, they may come to fourscore years;
verses.11: Yet is their pride but labour and sorrow: / so soon passeth it away, and we are gone.
verses.12: But who regardeth the power of thy wrath, / or feareth aright thine indignation?
verses.13: So teach us to number our days, / that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
